newsitem.title: USA: Cooper cites comfort with FY97 estimates.
newsitem.headline: Cooper cites comfort with FY97 estimates.

text.p: The Cooper Companies on Wednesday reported sharply higher income for the second quarter of 1997, expressing confidence it would meet analysts' expectations of earnings for this fiscal year.

"For the full fiscal year, I remain comfortable with the previous estimate of $1.45 to $1.55 per share, excluding an estimated 15 cents per share for deferred tax benefits, and with our estimate of $2.00 per share for 1998 before any deferred tax benefits," said chief executive officer Thomas Bender.
For the three months ended April 30, 1997, the company reported net income of $5.4 million, or 44 cents per share, including 4 cents per share for deferred tax benefits.
That compares with $2.8 million, or 24 cents per share, for the same quarter of 1996 when Cooper had not yet recorded any deferred tax benefits, the company said.

"Each of our operating businesses delivered solid revenue growth compared with last year's second quarter," Bender said, with sales at CooperVision (CVI), the specialty contact lens business, growing 22 percent both for the quarter and year to date.
In the first half of fiscal 1997, Cooper cited net income of $8.7 million, or 72 cents per share, compared to $3.5 million, or 30 cents per share, for the comparable 1996 period.

It said the 1997 results include deferred tax benefits of 7 cents per share, with operating income rising by 80 percent from $5.8 million in 1996 to $10.4 million in 1997. Revenue for the six-month period increased 27 percent to $62.0 million, Cooper said.
